rules.purpose: Base class for all spell statement rules.

Eats all whitespace at start of tokens -- used to skip leading indent/newlines before a real rule.

Indent whitespace specifically, e.g. leading spaces/tabs at start of a line.
Single newline.
Inline whitespace only, e.g. spaces/tabs between tokens on same line.

Boolean literal -- also accepts common synonyms like `yes`/`no`, `ok`/`cancel`, `always`/`never`.
Literal `text` string.

Single word variable name, known or unknown.

A known variable of several words, read, e.g. `start pile`, `the test card` (epic page `outline-spell`, P26).
`it` LEFT OUT, before `is`, where the language drops its subject (epic `spanish` J96).

rules.purpose: A number written in hex, e.g. `1F0A0`, `ff`, `A0` -- the digits of `hex 1F0A0`.
A code point written in hex, e.g. `1F0A0`, `2665`, `A0` (epic page `outline-spell`, P26).
`the absolute value of {expression}`.

rules.purpose: `the biggest`/`largest` [thing] `of`/`in` {expression}, e.g. `largest of the prices`.
`the smallest` [thing] `of`/`in` {expression}, e.g. `smallest of prices`.
`round {expression}`, optionally `off`/`up`/`down`, e.g. `round price up`.
`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` comparison, e.g. `salary > expenses`.
`is greater than` or `is less than`, optionally `... or equal to`.
`plus` / `+`, e.g. `price + tax` -- `Precedence.sum`: tighter than comparisons, looser than `*` `/`.
`minus` / `-`, e.g. `price - tax`.
`*` / `times`, e.g. `price * taxRate` -- `Precedence.product`, tightest, alongside `/`.
`/` / `divided by`, e.g. `price / taxRate` -- `Precedence.product`, same as `*`.
Base for rules which READ a member off an object or `it`, e.g. `the short rank of the card`, `its suit`.
`the {member words} of {thing}` ~== `thing.member`.

rules.purpose: `the {member words}` inside an action, reading a property of the thing the action runs on, e.g. `shuffle the stock` => `this.stock.shuffle()` (epic `language`, P2).
`its {member words}`, where the words name a PROPERTY `it`'s type declares: the LONGEST run of them that does, e.g. `short rank` in `its short rank + its short suit`.

obtener una nueva card

rules.purpose: `its {property}` -- possessive shorthand.
`its {ordinal} {arg}` -- possessive-plus-ordinal shorthand, e.g. `its third card`.
1..N words naming a member, e.g. `short rank`, `short-rank`, `rank`.
A member's bare name starting a line of a type's outline body, e.g. `suit` in `- suit is a suit of its deck` (epic page `outline-spell`, P9).
A member's name in quotes, where it's being declared: `its "suit" is one of ...` in an outline-style type's body -- the outline style's "quotes teach a new word" (epic page `outline-spell`).
Single object-literal property declaration: `{property} (=|is|of) {value:expression}`.
`name T1` -- a one-word property and a bare name, no `=` (epic `outline-spell` P19).
`jokers` -- a property's name alone, meaning `jokers = yes` (epic `outline-spell` P26).
Object literal -- creates an object with one or more property values, e.g. `foo = 1 and bar is 2`.
ONE word naming a property: initial-lower-case, not one of the language's own words (its `blacklist`).
In an event's handler, who it concerns (epic `elemental-spell` P9, Q26).
The mouse and the keys, readable anywhere -- core's `input`, `input.ts`.
Fires a global event, optionally with a `props` object.

una partida es una aplicación donde:
	- su barra de menú es "menú del juego"

rules.purpose: `a card "is a (rank) of (suits)" for its ranks and its suits`.

syntaxes.example: una card "es un (rango)" para sus rangos

rules.purpose: The name of one thing, written bare after its type (epic `drawable-thing` P19).
A PATTERN in quotes, a regular expression, read exactly as typed.
What to say when a property's rule is broken, in place of the rule's own words.
What a property's value must be, the words after `must`, e.g. `not be empty`.

syntaxes.syntax: (empty:no debe estar vacío|no debe estar vacio|no debe estar vacía|no debe estar vacia) {suggestion:rule_suggestion}?

rules.purpose: Makes a property text that must be a web address or an email address.
In an outline line, makes a property text that must be a url or an email.
Adds to a type declared elsewhere, in the outline style -- `a game:`, then bullets about games (epic page `outline-spell`, P11).
What a list does on the page as a thing is dragged over it, out of it, or dropped on it.
People may reorder a list's items on the page, by dragging them (epic `outline-spell` P30).
In a type's outline body, a list of values which is a KIND of thing of its own, kept by the type the body is about.
How a type draws, in its outline body (epic `spanish` P20).
A view's SLOTS, the named drawings it places (epic `elemental-spell` P5, Q55, Q56; P27).
In a drawing's body, a line of markup IS what it draws -- no `return` (epic `elemental-spell` P5, Q14).
What a property's value must be, beyond its type, said on a line of its own.
What a property's value must be, said indented under the property's own line.
`the color of a card` -- one of two `type_property` spellings, read by `property_value_either` and `property_value_getter`.
`its "color"` in an outline body -- the third `type_property` spelling.
RETIRED words for waiting, as spell waits by itself (epic `language` P13, Q9): `await`/`wait for` an expression, with the expression itself optional (bare `await`).
Check whether a conceptual animation or process is currently running.
Delay for a certain amount of time, e.g. `pause for 2 seconds`.
Runs its lines together, and carries on once they've all ended.

syntaxes.example:
para do something
	al mismo tiempo:
		imprimir 1
		imprimir 2

py.code:
def do_something() -> None:
    core.together(lambda: print(1), lambda: print(2))

rules.purpose: Starts something and carries on, with no waiting for it: `meanwhile deal the cards`.

syntaxes.example:
para do something
	mientras tanto imprimir 1

rules.purpose: Start a conceptual animation or process, e.g. `start animation dealing`.
Stop a conceptual animation or process.
Draw a single thing, e.g. `draw the card`.
Draw each / all of a collection of items.

syntaxes.example: dibujar cada carta en el deck

rules.purpose: Start a scoped `App`/`View`, e.g. `start the game` => `game.start()` (a method call, not a global).
Base for JSX rules which parse spell out of their token's text: `jsxAttribute` values and `jsxExpression`s.
Formatted text in a drawing, drawn by Spell UI's `<ui-markdown>` (epic `drawable-thing`, P14).

syntaxes.example:
<markdown>
	## Klondike
	Build each pile **down**, alternating colours.
</markdown>

js.code: h("ui-markdown", "## Klondike\nBuild each pile **down**, alternating colours.")

py.code: h("ui-markdown", "## Klondike\nBuild each pile **down**, alternating colours.")

rules.purpose: A notebook's EXAMPLE, in a drawing (epic `elemental-spell` P16): a title, then its live result, drawn by the editor app's `<spell-example>`.
Match a JSX element (`<tag attr=.../>` or `<tag>...</tag>`) as an `expression`/`jsxChild`.
Several elements drawn side by side, with no element around them, `<>...</>`.
Match literal text between JSX tags (`jsxChild`).
Match a JSX closing tag (`</tag>`), tracked as a `jsxChild` alongside element/text/expression children.

Match a `{...}` JSX expression container (a `jsxChild`, e.g. `
{1 + 2}
`).
A comment among markup's children, never drawn (epic `elemental-spell`, Owen 2026-10-26).
Match a single JSX attribute (`name`, `name=value`, or `name={expression}`).
Base pattern rule for matching a type name, singular or plural, known or unknown.
`it` in an outline-style type's body: the type the body is about, e.g. `Card` in `- it has a deck` under `a card is a thing where:`.
Possibly-unknown type identifier, singular or plural, e.g. `thing` or `things` => `Thing`.
Possibly-unknown type identifier which MUST be singular -- fails on plural input.
Possibly-unknown type identifier which MUST be plural -- fails on singular input.
A type's name in quotes, where it's being declared, e.g. `a "card" is a thing where:` -- the outline style's "quotes teach a new word" (epic page `outline-spell`).
Known type identifier, NOT including built-in types like `Object`.
The name a declaration gives a type, one word or several, e.g. `bank account` in `a bank account is a thing`.
A value kind's name of several words, singular, naming one of its values (epic `spanish` P22).
`it`, as the subject of an outline body's line, e.g. `- it has a deck` -- see `SubjectRule`.
`its`, as the subject of an outline body's line, e.g. `- its "suit" is ...` -- see `SubjectRule`.
The subject an outline body's line leaves out (epic page `outline-spell`, P8).
Assignment, via any of 4 equivalent surface forms: `{thing} = {value}`, `let {thing} = {value}`, `set {thing} to {value}`, or `{variable} is {value}`.

syntaxes.example: bob es una nueva person cuyo name es "bob"

js.code: export const bob = new Person({ name: "bob" })

ts.code: export const bob = new Person({ name: "bob" })

rules.purpose: `set start pile to ...` -- sets, or declares, a variable of several words (epic page `outline-spell`, P26).
`get {value}` -- assign `value` to a NEW `it`.
`(return|exit with?) {expression}? {nested_expression}?` -- return a value.
A no-op statement -- compiles to `core.doNothing()`.
A spellx closer on its own line, `</>` or `</property>` (epic `elemental-spell` P6).
`(else|otherwise) if {condition} (then|:)?` -- else-if branch, chained after `if`.
`(else|otherwise) :?` -- else branch.
`if {condition} (then|:)?` statement, with an inline statement or an indented nested block as body.
Postfix ternary, `{expr} if {condition} (else|otherwise) {expr}`.
`red if it is diamonds or hearts` -- one line of a getter's body: a VALUE, then when it's the answer.

syntaxes.example:
para elegir un color:
	red si suit es "hearts"

rules.purpose: `black otherwise` -- the value when no `value_if` line above was the answer: `return 'black'`.

syntaxes.example:
para elegir un color:
	black de lo contrario

rules.purpose: Print an expression (to the console currently).
Stop a previous `print group...`
Tells the person something for a moment, in a toast, e.g. `notify "Saved!"`.

syntaxes.syntax: notificar {kind:notify_kind}? {message:expression} (titulado {title:expression})? (en {color:toast_color} (inverted:invertido|invertida)?)? {position:toast_position}? ((durante {time:expression} {units:pause_units})|(untilClicked:hasta un clic|hasta que se haga clic))? {progress:toast_progress}? (sideBySide:uno al lado del otro|en fila)? (keepRunning:sin pausa|sin pausar)? (con {okButton:text})? (y esperar)?

rules.purpose: Show user a `message` in a modal alert.
Warning message -- like alert but more dire.
Confirm message -- present a question with two answers.
Prompt user to specify a value in response to `message` with `defaultValue`.
Parse CSS from a `TextToken` WITHOUT quotes.
Rule `constructor` for a plain (non-instance, non-operator) dynamically-defined method's CALL SITE, e.g. matching `notify 1` after `to notify (message): ...` defined it.
Base for method-DEFINITION rules built on `method_signature`: `to_do_something`, `create_animation` and `quoted_type_expression`.
`card nerds out with thing`: calls a quoted method defined as an infix expression: e.g. `card.nerdsOutWithAnother(thing)`.
`card is face up` -- reads a quoted method defined as a postfix expression, e.g. `card.isFaceUp`.
Defines a new method/statement: e.g. `to foo the bar`, `to create a card`, `to create (a card)`, `to notify (message)`.
RETIRED words for an action, as spell waits by itself (epic `language` P13, Q9): `animation deal the cards`, or `create animation deal the cards`.
Defines an ad-hoc expression on a type from a QUOTED signature, e.g. `a thing "nerds out" if`, `a thing "is a bug" if`, `a thing "nerds out with (another as a thing)" if`.

syntaxes.example:
una cosa "se luce" si
si una nueva cosa se luce

rules.purpose: What runs as a thing is made, in its type's outline, e.g. `- when created (with title as text):`.

syntaxes.example:
una tarea es una cosa donde:
	- al crearla (con título como texto, hecha como una opción):
		imprimir el título

rules.purpose: One line of an ACTION's description, said indented under it (epic `elemental-spell` P5).

syntaxes.example:
una carta es una cosa donde:
	- su dirección es una de arriba o abajo
	- para voltearla:
		- atajo meta+T
		- activa cuando su dirección es abajo
		- se deshace como "Voltear carta"
		poner su dirección en arriba

rules.purpose: One bare word in a method's keyword phrase, e.g. `foo`, `the`, `bar` in `to foo the bar`.
Untyped variable inside parens, e.g. `(message)` in `to notify (message): ...`.
Variable arg with a default value, e.g. `(message = "Really?")` in `to notify (message = "Really?"): ...`.
Bare type name inside parens, e.g. `(a card)` in `to create (a card): ...`.
Variable arg with explicit type, e.g. `(thing as a card)` in `to show (thing as a card): ...`.
A `with`-prefixed prop list.
A KNOWN type after `a` / `an`, with no parens, in a method's signature: a parameter, as `(a card)` is.
A full method signature, alternating keywords and args.
A QUOTED phrase's words, where only `(...)` is a parameter (epic page `outline-spell`, P26).
Method signature surrounded by quotes.
ONE keyboard shortcut, written as its keys joined by `+`, no spaces: `meta+T`, `meta+shift+Z`, `F2`, `meta+,` (epic `elemental-spell` P5).
An assertion -- `expect {expression}`, `expect {expression} to be {value}` or `{expression} should be {value}`.

syntaxes.example: esperar que el rank de it sea "queen"

rules.purpose: `echo {expression}` -- print `expression`'s value, e.g. for debugging.
`start test {message}` or `start quiet test {message}` -- marks beginning of a named test run.
`end test` -- marks end of the current named test run started by `start_test`.
